title: Formatting cells with the keyboard
summary: Make text bold, italic or underlined, show numbers as currency or percentages, and open the Format Cells window.
intro:
Formatting does not change the value stored in a cell, only the way it is shown. The number 0.25 is still 0.25 even when you show it as 25%.

The font shortcuts (bold, italic, underline) are the same in most programs. The number-format shortcuts use Ctrl and Shift with the format's own symbol: `$` for currency and `%` for percent.

faq.q: How do I turn bold off?
faq.a: Press the same shortcut again. Bold, italic and underline each switch on and off.

faq.q: Which currency does the currency shortcut use?
faq.a: The currency of your computer's settings. To choose another one, open the Format Cells window and pick the currency in the Number section.

bold.prompt: You selected the table headings. To make them bold, press `Ctrl+B` (on Mac: `⌘+B`).

italic.prompt: To write a note in italics, press `Ctrl+I` (on Mac: `⌘+I`).

underline.prompt: To underline the text, press `Ctrl+U` (on Mac: `⌘+U`).

currency-format.prompt: You selected the price column. To show it in currency format, press `Ctrl+Shift+$` (the 4 key with Shift).
currency-format.hint: The dollar sign $ is above the 4.

percent-format.prompt: The next column holds rates such as 0.25. To show them as 25%, press `Ctrl+Shift+%` (the 5 key with Shift).
percent-format.hint: The percent sign % is above the 5.

format-cells-dialog.prompt: For every formatting option in one place, open the Format Cells window with `Ctrl+1` (on Mac: `⌘+1`). The browser uses this shortcut to switch tabs, so pick it from the list.
